newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia development tax break halt expected.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia development tax break halt expected.

text.p: The halt in tax break acceptances for Australian infrastructure bonds had been on the cards for sometime, according to Macquarie Bank.

Treasurer Peter Costello announced on Tuesday that he had directed the Development Allowance Authority (DAA) to accept no further applications for a tax break on infrastructure borrowing until July 1 next year.
"It's probably a good cooling off period for the market," said Nicholas Moore, executive director at Macquarie Bank.
Since the coalition government came to power in March there had been fears that this tax break would cease.
"It's been a self-fulfilling fear. Anyone who had a project that had a chance of going, lodged for approval for infrastructure bonds," Moore said.

Costello said on Tuesday that the DAA was currently assessing applications for total infrastructure borrowings of A$26.5 billion, seven times the value of applications actually approved since March 5, 1995 when applications were first invited.
Moore said he hoped that the government would come back in the not too distant future to make clear the government's thoughts on the issue of infrastructure debt.
"Once the market has certainty we won't see the number of applications going in recently, go in," Moore added.
A development allowance entitles a business to deduct 10 percent of the value of plant and equipment from its taxable income, in addition to any other entitlements.
Under the scheme, business can finance approved infrastructure projects with bonds that pay tax-free interest.
Costello said that the programme would cost the government a maximum of A$150 million in 1996/97.
